entries.notes: Official metadata: Traeuble F, von Kuegelgen J, Kleindessner M, Locatello F, Schoelkopf B, Gehler P. NeurIPS 34 (2021), pp. 116-128. Full text (main paper, no appendix) read: defines the Prediction Update Problem for STORED predictions on an unlabelled dataset; baseline Replace = backfilling (re-evaluate all stored predictions with newest model); metrics NF, NFR = sum NF/(N*T), PF/NF, and BTC/BEC from Srivastava et al.; attributes the term backward compatibility to Bansal et al. Classification only. Closest ML analogue of the paper retained-vs-reprocessed question.

entries.notes: Full text read. Defines locally and globally compatible updates and the compatibility score C(h1,h2)=sum_x A(x,h1(x))A(x,h2(x))/sum_x A(x,h1(x)) (Eq. 1); dissonance loss; Q3: h1 on 200 examples vs h2 on 5000 examples, compatibility as low as 40% (logistic regression, in-hospital mortality). Classification/actions only.

entries.notes: Cited anchor re-read at methods level (not a new paper): NFR = (1/N) sum 1(yhat_new != y, yhat_old = y) (Eq. 2); relative NFR = NFR/((1-ER_old)*ER_new) (Eq. 11). Two ResNet-152 runs with different initialisations: same 78.3% accuracy, differ on 10.4% of validation samples. entries.query: https://aclanthology.org/2021.acl-long.515.pdf
entries.notes: Full text read: R_NF(D_reg,f_old,f_new)=|{x: f_old=y, f_new!=y}|/|D_reg| following Yan et al.; frames measurement as software regression testing on a regression set D_reg; random-seed-only change gave up to 3.56% negative flips (BERT-base); proposes two continuous-space proxies for regression (KL divergence of predicted probabilities, l2 distance of representations) used as training penalties, not as compatibility metrics for continuous targets. No NFI defined here.

entries.query: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.02976 (Cai et al., cited anchor)
entries.notes: Cited anchor read at methods level: for structured outputs (graphs), negative flips are counted over graphs or sub-graphs under each accuracy metric (word-level UAS, tree-level UCM, span EM); NFR follows Yan et al.; Cai et al. INTRODUCE negative flip impact NFI = NFR/ER_new (proportion of new-model errors that are negative flips). Random-seed changes alone gave NFR >= 1.55%. Attributes first study of update regression to Shen et al. 2020 (Bansal 2019 and Milani Fard 2016 predate it).

entries.notes: Jiang, Narasimhan, Bahri, Cotter, Rostamizadeh. Churn Reduction via Distillation: arXiv 2106.02654v2, journal_ref ICLR 2022 and camera-ready header Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2022 (OpenReview v1 API returned a challenge, 403). Definition read: predictive churn = difference in prediction of a model relative to a base model on the same datapoints; ideal = fraction of disagreements; tractable soft churn = E_x[d(g(x),h(x))] for a divergence d between output distributions; evaluation uses hard churn. Bhojanapalli et al. 2021: arXiv 2102.03349v1 only (no venue in arXiv metadata); churn = disagreement between two independently trained models (abstract). OpenReview also listed SIGDIAL 2022 and EMNLP-Industry 2023 churn papers (screened, not kept).

entries.query: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.09435 ; GET https://api.crossref.org/works/10.18653/v1/2024.findings-emnlp.430
entries.notes: Echterhoff JM, Faghri F, Vemulapalli R, Hu T-Y, Li C-L, Tuzel O, Pouransari H. MUSCLE. Findings of EMNLP 2024, pp. 7320-7332. Full text (arXiv) read: extends compatibility metrics to CONTINUOUS evaluation scores: D(x_i)=S(M_v2(x_i),y_i)-S(M_v1(x_i),y_i) for a similarity metric S; PFR~=(1/N)sum 1[D>0], NFR~=(1/N)sum 1[D<0]; mean gain m_g and mean regression magnitude m_r=(1/(N NFR~)) sum |D| 1[D<0]; also NFR_mc counting flips when both models are wrong. Single-timepoint, per-instance quality scores; not a measurement-change or cross-version difference metric. Cites Matsuno and Sakuma 2023 (robust backward compatibility metric).

entries.query: arXiv id_list=2308.05619 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.05619 ; https://proceedings.mlr.press/v219/ (index) and https://proceedings.mlr.press/v219/otles23a/otles23a.pdf
entries.notes: Otles E, Denton BT, Wiens J. Updating Clinical Risk Stratification Models Using Rank-Based Compatibility. Proc. 8th Machine Learning for Healthcare Conference, PMLR 219:529-547 (2023). Full text read (arXiv and PMLR versions agree on the checked passages): C^R(f^o,f^u)=sum_{i in I0} sum_{j in I1} 1(p_i^o<p_j^o)1(p_i^u<p_j^u) / sum 1(p_i^o<p_j^o) (Eq. 3), the probability that the updated model ranks a discordant patient pair correctly given the original did; general form (Appendix Eq. 6) for any ordered labels, e.g. integer or real values; authors state rank concordance may be more robust to calibration shifts. Threshold-free compatibility for continuous outputs, but rank-based and single-timepoint: invariant to the monotone calibration shift that produces the paper retention cost.

entries.query: GET https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10952221/fullTextXML
entries.notes: Riley RD, Collins GS 2023 read at methods level. Section 3.2.3: MAPE for individual i = sum_b |p_bi - p_i| / B (mean absolute difference between bootstrap-model and original-model predictions); average MAPE = sum_b sum_i |p_bi - p_i| /(B N); four levels of stability from overall mean to individual; warns that the average masks individual-level differences. Case study: average MAPE 0.038 (all 27 predictors forced) vs 0.029 (LASSO). Precedent for an individual-level, model-to-model absolute-difference summary of continuous outputs.
